value.notes: Submitted when on; defaults to the native "on".

uncheckedValue.notes: Submitted when off; nothing is submitted by default.

nativeButton.notes: Root renders <span> so an enclosing <label> works; use nativeButton + render={<button />} for sibling labels.

id.notes: Applies to the hidden input; with nativeButton it applies to the root element instead.

dataAttributes: data-valid / data-invalid, data-dirty / data-touched, data-filled, data-focused (inside Field.Root)
Thumb emits the same set, which is how the translate-x animation is driven

renderProp.functionForm: render={(props, state) => {state.checked ? : }} — the composition handbook's canonical Switch.Thumb example

formIntegration.hiddenInput: Renders a hidden <input> beside the visible span; value is submitted when on, uncheckedValue when off (nothing by default).
formIntegration.validation: required is enforced natively; Field.Root name is the field key.

keyboard.keys: Native activation only (Space/Enter on the native button). No custom key map.
keyboard.focus: Single tab stop, focus ring via :focus-visible.

notableDifferences: React Aria's Switch uses isSelected/onChange; Base UI uses checked/defaultChecked/onCheckedChange, and role="switch" + aria-checked is applied by the component (React Aria's Switch does the same).
The moving part is an explicit Thumb part with its own data-checked attribute, instead of styling ::before/::after or the root.
React Aria has isPending/isDisabled; Base UI has disabled only.
State is data-attribute driven (data-checked on both Root and Thumb) rather than render-prop driven.
